10.0.0.en: Here he mentions the sons of the sons of Noah. These sons are the heads of the tribes and peoples that appeared in the world and are still present until now.

10.1.0.en: He begins with the descendants of Japheth, and some think he was the eldest son because Moses begins with him. His children settled in Europe and in some countries of Asia, and he begot seven sons, who are:

10.1.1.en: Gomer: his name means 'complete.' They first settled in Media and Gog, which are regions of Iran, then moved to northern Europe and Asia, and some of them migrated to Asia Minor, that is, Turkey.

10.1.2.en: Magog: they settled in the regions of the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea, and among them were the Scythians, from whom the Russians came. From them also came the Tatar people, who attacked the world in ancient times, and they are a symbol of those who oppose the people of God in the Book of Revelation (Rev 20:7-9). Madai: they settled south of the Caspian Sea and united with the kingdom of Persia in the sixth century B.C., and formed the empire of the Medes and Persians, which brought the children of Israel back from captivity.

10.1.3.en: Javan: that is, Greece, as it is mentioned in (Zech 9:13, Isa 66:19). Tubal: they lived in northern Iraq, then moved to the southeast of the Black Sea, and they traded in slaves.

10.1.4.en: Meshech: his name is linked with Tubal, and he lived in the same regions in which Tubal lived.

10.1.5.en: Tiras: they settled on the coasts and islands of the Aegean Sea.

10.1.6.en: As for Gomer, he begot three sons, who are:

10.1.7.en: 1- Ashkenaz: he settled east of the Black Sea in Armenia, and it is said that they are the origin of the German people.

10.1.8.en: 2- Riphath: his descendants were the Rephaim, who settled east of the Jordan.

10.1.9.en: 3- Togarmah: the origin of Armenia. They settled in the east of Asia Minor and the southwest of the Caspian Sea, and they traded in horses and mules, and they are mentioned in (Ezek 27:14, 26). As for Javan, he begot four sons, who are:

10.1.10.en: 1- Elishah: his descendants settled in Greece and Cyprus, and he is mentioned in (Ezek 27:7).

10.1.11.en: 2- Tarshish: his descendants settled in Italy and Spain, and they built their city in the south of Spain, to which Jonah the prophet fled (Jon 1:3).

10.1.12.en: 3- Kittim: his descendants settled in Cyprus and on the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea, and he is mentioned in (Num 24:24).

10.1.13.en: 4- Dodanim: his descendants settled on the island of Rhodes and in some parts of Greece.

10.1.14.en: Care for the upbringing of your children, for these children may later become the heads of families who spread the name of God or who become a curse to it. So do not be negligent in guiding them, caring for them, and binding them to the Church.

10.2.0.en: Here he mentions four sons of Ham, the first of whom is Cush.

10.2.1.en: A- Cush: the meaning of his name is black, and he had six sons, who are:

10.2.2.en: 1- Seba: he settled in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, then moved to the coasts of the Red Sea, the regions of Ethiopia, next to Sheba, his nephew.

10.2.3.en: 2- Havilah: he settled in the north of the land of the Arabs and all its country.

10.2.4.en: 3- Sabtah: his descendants settled in Hadramaut in the Arabian Peninsula, then some of them moved to Abyssinia.

10.2.5.en: 4- Raamah: he traded in gold, precious things, and spices (Ezek 27:22), and he had two sons, who are: Sheba: he settled in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, then moved to Ethiopia.

10.2.6.en: Dedan: he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs, then moved to some of their countries.

10.2.7.en: 5- Sabtechah: he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs.

10.3.0.en: 6- Nimrod: his name means a mighty one or a rebel. He mentions him alone because of his distinction in strength. He worked in hunting wild beasts and was an innovator, and he became a proverb for strength and rebellion. He founded a kingdom that included these places: Babel: its name means the gate of God, and God called it so because the confusion of tongues took place in it when the tower was built (ch. 11:9). It lies on the river Euphrates and was the capital of the Babylonian kingdom in the seventh century B.C. Erech: it lies east of the Euphrates.

10.3.1.en: Accad: it lies west of the river Tigris.

10.3.2.en: Calneh: it lies east of the Euphrates, north of Erech.

10.4.0.en: Out of that land went forth Asshur: the meaning is that Nimrod went out from the land of his kingdom to Asshur, the son of his cousin Shem, and built there the city of Nineveh, that is, the place of the god Nin, on the river Tigris. Then he built to the south of it a spacious city called Rehoboth-Ir. Then he went south again and built the city of Calah, then he built the city of Resen between Nineveh and Calah.

10.4.1.en: The great city: it is the city of Nineveh.

10.5.0.en: B- Mizraim: the second son of Ham (v. 6), who settled in Egypt, North Africa, and Palestine. His sons are:

10.5.1.en: 1- Ludim: he settled west of the Nile and in North Africa, in the regions of Libya.

10.5.2.en: 2- Anamim: he settled in the Nile Delta.

10.5.3.en: 3- Lehabim: that is, the flaming ones. They settled in Libya and are mentioned under the name Lubims (2 Chr 12:3).

10.5.4.en: 4- Naphtuhim: he settled in Middle Egypt, toward Memphis.

10.5.5.en: 5- Pathrusim: that is, the land of the south. He settled in Upper Egypt, that is, the Sa'id, and their capital was Thebes (Luxor.)

10.5.6.en: 6- Casluhim: he settled east of the Delta next to the Mediterranean Sea and as far as the regions of Palestine. Two sons came out of him, who are:

10.5.7.en: - Philistim: he is the origin of the Philistines.

10.5.8.en: - Caphtorim: he settled in the Delta near Memphis.

10.5.9.en: C- Phut: the third son of Ham, mentioned in (v. 6), and he settled in the regions of Libya. His sons are probably not mentioned because of their lack of importance.

10.6.0.en: D- Canaan: the fourth son of Ham (v. 6). He settled next to the Mediterranean Sea and in the land of Palestine, and his sons are:

10.6.1.en: 1- Sidon: his name means fishing, and his city, which is named after him, lies on the Mediterranean Sea, north of Tyre and south of Beirut, and its inhabitants were famous for catching fish.

10.6.2.en: 2- Heth: he settled in Hebron, north of Iraq, and Abraham dwelt beside them and bought from them a field in which he buried his wife Sarah (Gen 23:5).

10.6.3.en: 3- The Jebusite: they are the original inhabitants of Jerusalem. Joshua took their land, and afterward David, where he established his city (2 Sam 5:8).

10.6.4.en: 4- The Amorites: that is, the mountain dwellers, because they lived in the mountains south of Jerusalem and west of the Dead Sea, and Joshua drove them out (Josh 10:5).

10.6.5.en: 5- The Girgasite: he settled east of the Sea of Galilee, and Joshua drove them out (Josh 3:10).

10.6.6.en: 6- The Hivite: he settled in the northeast of Palestine, and among their cities was Shechem.

10.6.7.en: 7- The Arkite: they settled in Lebanon.

10.6.8.en: 8- The Sinite: they settled next to their brothers the Arkites.

10.6.9.en: 9- The Arvadite: that is, a wanderer, because his sons used to travel about, and they first settled on the island of Arvad in the Mediterranean, next to Homs.

10.6.10.en: 10- The Zemarite: his name means the mountain dweller, and he settled on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea in Lebanon.

10.6.11.en: 11- The Hamathite: that is, the strong one. He settled in Hamath, north of Damascus in Syria.

10.7.0.en: Here he mentions the borders of the dwelling place of the sons of Canaan, which are:

10.7.1.en: From the north: Sidon and Hamath.

10.7.2.en: From the south: Gaza and Gerar.

10.7.3.en: From the east: Sodom and Gomorrah.

10.7.4.en: From the west: the Mediterranean Sea.

10.7.5.en: Canaan had many sons, but because they were cursed by Noah, Joshua drove them out on account of their evil. So do not be preoccupied with the abundance of your wealth, your sons, or your possessions, for all of them pass away if you do not abide in God. Do not rely on them, use them only for the need of the body, and with them do mercy to all who are around you.

10.8.0.en: All the children of Eber: Eber is one of the grandsons of Shem, and because of his importance he is mentioned here alone, since from him came Abraham, the father of the Hebrews, that is, the people of God, and also the father of the Arabs, whose head is Ishmael. The brother of Japheth the elder: there are two opinions about the word 'the elder.' Either it is a description of Shem, so that he would be the firstborn of Noah, or a description of Japheth, so that he would be the firstborn.

10.9.0.en: Shem begot five sons, who are:

10.9.1.en: 1- Elam: he settled north of the Persian Gulf, that is, present-day Iran.

10.9.2.en: 2- Asshur: he settled by the river Tigris, then established an empire that included all the lands surrounding him. It was the second empire in the world after Egypt, and it lasted a long time.

10.9.3.en: 3- Arphaxad: the ancestor of the Arab tribes and also of the Chaldeans, who settled between the two rivers in Iraq, and from his descendants came Abraham, the father of the fathers.

10.9.4.en: 4- Lud: the father of nomadic tribes that finally settled in the south of Asia Minor.

10.9.5.en: 5- Aram: he formed a great kingdom, which is ancient Syria, and its capital was Damascus.

10.10.0.en: Here he mentions the sons of Aram, that is, the grandsons of Shem, and they are:

10.10.1.en: 1- Uz: he settled in the region between Syria and Edom, and the righteous Job dwelt in his land (Job 1:1).

10.10.2.en: 2- Hul: he settled in the Jordan valley, north of the Sea of Galilee.

10.10.3.en: 3- Gether: he settled in the mountains of Lebanon and the north of the land of the Arabs.

10.10.4.en: 4- Mash: he settled in the mountains of Syria.

10.11.0.en: He mentions a son of Arphaxad, who is Salah, from whom Eber came, and this last one is of special importance because from him came Abraham and all the Hebrew people. The discussion about him will come in detail in (ch. 11).

10.12.0.en: Here he mentions two sons of Eber, who are:

10.12.1.en: 1- Peleg: his name means division. There was a crowding between his descendants and the descendants of his brother Joktan, so he settled in the region of the Tigris and the Euphrates, and from his descendants came Abraham.

10.12.2.en: The father of Peleg, who is Cainan, who is mentioned in the genealogy of Christ (Lk 3), is not mentioned, because of his lack of importance.

10.12.3.en: 2- Joktan: he settled in the land of the Arabs after separating from his brother Peleg.

10.13.0.en: Here he mentions the sons of Joktan, the father of the Arabs, and they are:

10.13.1.en: 1- Almodad: he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs.

10.13.2.en: 2- Sheleph: he also settled in the south of the land of the Arabs.

10.13.3.en: 3- Hazarmaveth: he settled in the southwest of the land of the Arabs.

10.13.4.en: 4- Jerah: they are the tribe of the Banu Hilal, and they settled in the east of the Arabian Peninsula.

10.13.5.en: 5- Hadoram: his descendants were fire worshipers, and they settled in the southwest of the Arabian Peninsula.

10.13.6.en: 6- Uzal: he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs and built the city of Azal, which is Sana'a in Yemen.

10.13.7.en: 7- Diklah: his name means a palm tree, and they settled in Yemen, where palm trees abound.

10.13.8.en: 8- Obal: he settled in Yemen and other places in the land of the Arabs.

10.13.9.en: 9- Abimael: he settled in the east of the land of the Arabs.

10.13.10.en: 10- Sheba: he settled in Yemen, and from him came the queen of Sheba who visited Solomon (1 Kgs 10).

10.13.11.en: 11- Ophir: he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs, and his land was famous for pure gold (1 Kgs 9:28).

10.13.12.en: 12- Havilah: he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs.

10.13.13.en: 13- Jobab: he settled in the east of the land of the Arabs.

10.14.0.en: The preceding tribes, the sons of Joktan, settled in the Arabian Peninsula, and here he mentions two places, one in the east of the land of the Arabs and the other in its west, and they are:

10.14.1.en: 1- Mesha: that is, Maysan, which lies on the northwestern edge of the Persian Gulf.

10.14.2.en: 2- Sephar, a mount of the east: it lies east of Hadramaut.

10.15.0.en: He concludes that these are the descendants of Shem and of his brothers Ham and Japheth, and the attached maps show the places of their dwelling (maps 1, 2, 3).

10.15.1.en: You notice that he focuses on some names and passes over others because of their lack of importance, and he focuses on Eber because from him came Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob ... Do you have a life with God that gives you a name that lasts forever in heaven and a great place among the saints?

10.15.2.en: Care for your relationship with God and your love for others before any material matter.

11.0.0.en: The descendants of Noah lived in places close to one another and spoke one language, most likely Hebrew, though some say it was Chaldean or Semitic.

11.1.0.en: Shinar: the plain of the Tigris and the Euphrates.

11.1.1.en: The ark rested on Mount Ararat, which lies northwest of the plain of Shinar, then they journeyed eastward into the region of Shinar.

11.2.0.en: Brick: that is, mud brick made of clay and straw.

11.2.1.en: Burn them thoroughly: baked with fire to become more durable.

11.2.2.en: Slime: a kind of mineral bitumen found in abundance in the region of the Tigris and the Euphrates, used to stick bricks to one another, instead of the clay used in ancient times or the cement used today.

11.2.3.en: The sons of Noah thought of building a city and houses. In ancient times they used to make mud bricks by mixing clay with straw, and they discovered that when mud brick is burned with fire it becomes stronger, so they made the red brick known today for building houses. And instead of using clay to stick the bricks to one another, they discovered in the region where they lived the substance of slime, which is a substance that sticks the bricks to one another with greater hardness.

11.3.0.en: A city: that is, a kingdom.

11.3.1.en: A name: renown and a great standing.

11.3.2.en: Although God had reassured Noah and his descendants that He would not destroy the world again by a flood, when they discovered by their minds, which God had given them, the means of making strong buildings with red brick and slime, they relied on their own strength to set up a kingdom and a high structure, which is the tower, so that if God thought of making a flood they would go up to the tower and the wrath of God would not frighten them. Thus they left God and depended on themselves, confident of their strength, to form a kingdom and a lasting center, and by this they neglected God, the heavenly city, and Paradise from which they had gone out and to which God will restore them if they live with Him in faith. St. Augustine believes that the leader of this work was Nimrod, who tried to found the city of Babylon, and who was mentioned before in (ch. 10:8-10).

11.4.0.en: The Lord came down: it is a declaration that He watches all our works, and it does not mean that He moved from one place to another, for He fills every place. His watching the city and the tower which they had begun to build is a proof of their pride, for which He will judge them, and of their refusal to rely on God.

11.5.0.en: There was a small city called Babel, which Nimrod had built, and now he was trying to enlarge it and build a high tower in it, so they began to use their new discovery, red brick and slime, in building. God did not forcibly prevent them from carrying out their pride, but out of pity for them, that they might repent and return to Him, He intervened in a simple way to stop the pride represented in the building of the tower.

11.6.0.en: Let us go down: it proclaims the Holy Trinity, because His speech is in the plural form, and it signifies the condescension of Christ by His Incarnation to lift the sin of man and his pride from him by redemption.

11.6.1.en: Let us confound: He made them speak different languages, that is, tongues.

11.6.2.en: God intervened to stop people from continuing further in evil, so that they might feel their weakness and return with Him to their spiritual life. So He made each group speak a language different from the other group, which made understanding between them impossible, and consequently they were unable to complete their plan of building the tower and the kingdom.

11.7.0.en: As a result of their inability to understand one another, each group speaking a certain language scattered to its own place. Thus they returned and carried out the word of God which He had said to them previously, that they should be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth. In this way the beginnings of the tribes were formed, which later founded the nations and kingdoms.

11.8.0.en: God called the name of the city Babel, in the sense of the confusion of tongues, so it became a proof of human pride, for which the merciful God was compelled to change their languages in order to rescue them from pride.

11.8.1.en: Pride is the first sin of man and the cause of the fall of Satan, and Satan still fights humanity, not only in the days of the Tower of Babel but even now, with pride ... So be careful of it: thank God for all that you do, put others before yourself, bear their offenses, and extinguish their fires with your love for them.
